item.description: Solve frustrating CORS policy connection blocks across modern web applications, reverse proxies, and embedded ESP32 microcontrollers with this guide.

item.description: An exhaustive, publication-grade engineering guide to troubleshooting HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor connection issues with ESP32, covering 5V/3.3V logic level shifting, safe GPIO selection, and time-of-flight debugging.

item.title: How to Write Code That Anyone Can Read and Maintain
item.description: An exhaustive, publication-grade software engineering guide on clean code architecture, maintainability standards, descriptive naming conventions, modular design, and documentation best practices.

item.title: ESP32 Won't Wake from Deep Sleep: Causes and Fixes
item.description: Deep sleep is the single most useful feature of a battery ESP32 — and the one that trips up the most people. If your board never wakes, wakes instantly, or drains a 18650 in three days, one of the six causes below is almost certainly the reason.

item.title: Driving a DC Motor from an ESP32 with a Low-Side MOSFET
item.description: An ESP32 pin can only supply a few milliamps, so it can never power a motor directly. A logic-level MOSFET turns the pin into a safe, fast electronic switch and lets you control speed with PWM.

item.title: Fixing Relay Chatter When Switching AC Loads from an ESP32
item.description: A relay that buzzes, clicks repeatedly, or resets your ESP32 is almost never a broken relay. It is a power, isolation or snubber problem. Fix those three and the circuit becomes as reliable as any commercial smart switch.

item.title: Why Your ESP32 Wi-Fi Keeps Dropping (and How to Fix It Permanently)
item.description: An ESP32 that connects once, then drops, reconnects, or loses packets is rarely a faulty chip. In almost every case, the cause is one of five things: weak power, bad antenna placement, wrong Wi-Fi power-save settings, a missing reconnect routine, or interference from your own 2.4 GHz network.

item.title: Why Your LED Strip Flickers: PWM, Power and Ground Explained
item.description: An LED strip that flickers, dims unevenly or shows random colours is telling you one of four things: not enough power, too much voltage drop, a data signal that is too weak, or a ground that is not shared. Each has a different fix, and each is measurable in minutes.

item.title: Turn a 2015 Laptop into a Fast Machine: SSD + RAM Upgrade Guide
item.description: A laptop with an i5-5200U and 4 GB RAM is not slow because the CPU is old — it is slow because it is waiting for a 5400 rpm hard drive and swapping to disk. Replacing those two parts costs less than a new laptop and gives 10× the responsiveness.

item.title: PC Won't Boot? The 7-Step No-POST Checklist
item.description: The fans spin, the LEDs light up, but there is no display and no beep. Before you assume the motherboard is dead, strip the system down to the minimum and let it tell you what is wrong.

item.title: Stop Your Raspberry Pi from Overheating in a Closed Case
item.description: A Raspberry Pi inside a sealed 3D-printed box will happily hit 85 °C under load, throttle itself to 600 MHz, and feel "slow" without ever crashing. The fix is not a bigger heatsink — it is understanding airflow, thermal mass and the throttle flags the Pi already reports.

item.title: Router Keeps Rebooting? 6 Causes You Can Fix Today
item.description: A router that reboots itself is usually telling you the power supply is dying, the firmware is buggy, or the DHCP table is full. Only one of those requires buying a new router.
